title: Why Cats Always Land on Their Feet
board: Hook: the cat walks along the top of the bookcase
A back paw slips: over it goes
Rewind to the moment it left the shelf
X-ray scan of the ear: the balance organ
The crystals slide toward the real ground
Signal: ear > brain > spinal cord > legs
It bends in the middle: bendy chest spine
Front legs tucked: the front half turns
Back half follows, about 80 ms later
Silence: upright, legs out, back arched
Kitten at 3 weeks: half a turn, a flop
Low stool vs high shelf: time to turn?
Full speed again; it walks off, kitten follows
